loci.name: fleet-service-model-by-host-class
loci.one_line: How does the user-service vs system-service fight resolve per host class: can one declarative NixOS module ship both variants, and can a system-scoped (or lingered-user) agent reach the session/user bus that the niri and notification backends need on headless hosts?
loci.rationale: The contradiction graph's 'this IS the every-host question' cluster, whose own evidence_quality_delta admits it reconciles 'by host-class, not by winner' — but the corpus never works out the reconciliation. Side B's structural evidence for servers: what-is-the-difference-between-systemdservices-and-systemduserservices-help-nixo documents that NixOS-installed user units do NOT restart on nixos-rebuild switch; systemduser-archwiki states user units cannot order after system units and run outside logind sessions; enabling-persistent-user-instance-systemd-issue-3702-nixosnixpkgs-github shows the 9-year declarative-linger gap (closed only Oct 2023, PR #260248 → nixosusers-groups-add-user-option-to-ena). Side A's practical evidence for kiosks: session-bus-dependent backends need the user manager (github-z-galaxyzbus-rust-d-bus-crate-github assumes DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS; openclaw-gateway-status-fails-on-ec2headless-servers-due-to-missing-user-level-s documents the exact 'No medium found' failure ladder on headless boxes). Genuinely unresolved depth questions the corpus only gestures at: (a) the shape of a services.ha-agent NixOS module that ships a system unit on servers and a user unit on kiosks via mkIf per host class (extend-nixos-official-nixos-wiki shows the module pattern but nobody applies it to this fork); (b) whether on modern systemd the user bus at /run/user/<uid>/bus — which exists under linger with no graphical session — is reachable by a system service with User=io, making set-up-systemd-services-with-session-dbus-on-headless-linux-baeldung-on-linux's manual dbus.socket craft unnecessary; (c) verifying the nixos-rebuild-switch restart gap is still true on current NixOS for user units, since the source thread is Feb 2023; (d) how the module delivers MQTT credentials and TLS (nixos-manual documents mosquitto ACL deny-all + TLS listener options; flakes-official-nixos-wiki warns store is world-readable; the agent's tls knob is a verified dead defect). Decides whether europa and callisto can run the agent at all.

opposing_positions.position: User service + linger is the fleet-native shape: no root needed, go-hass-agent refuses root entirely, jupiterOS already ships ConditionUser=io + users.users.io.linger, and desktop backends (niri IPC, notifications) get the session bus for free.

System service (optionally User=/AmbientCapabilities=) is the fleet-native shape: user units don't restart on nixos-rebuild switch, cannot order after system units, need linger configured per user on every host, and hit 'No medium found' bus failures headless — servers need a system unit.

suggested_searches: systemd user bus /run/user/uid/bus without session linger
system service connect to user bus unix:path=/run/user
NixOS systemd.user.services restart on nixos-rebuild switch current
NixOS systemd service AmbientCapabilities example
sops-nix agenix MQTT credentials systemd service

loci.name: adopt-vs-build-verdict
loci.one_line: Improve ha-linux-agent or adopt go-hass-agent/lnxlink: what exact capability and fleet-integration delta justifies a custom Rust agent once the honest line-by-line comparison (including the incumbents' NixOS-module absence, split-brain identity, and headless behaviour) is done?
loci.rationale: The user said 'improve it', but go-hass-agent-mynixos proves a mature agent (v14.15.1) is one package line away in nixpkgs proper, and lnxlink documents ~50 modules — an advocate-register report must argue improve-vs-adopt or its roadmap is question-begging. The corpus holds both sides without ever doing the comparison the required comparison table needs. Side A (adopt): go-hass-agent-mynixos + go-hass-agent-a-native-app-integration-for-desktop-laptop-devices-share-your-proj + github-bkbillylnxlink-effortlessly-manage-your-linux-machine-using-mqtt-github. Side B (build): github-joshuargo-hass-agent-a-home-assistant-native-app-for-desktoplaptop-device itself documents go-hass-agent's weaknesses — MQTT v5 hard requirement, HA-side split-brain (one device appears twice: mobile_app AND MQTT, cannot be combined), no state sync for custom controls, raw hwmon without chip scaling — while ha-linux-agent's differentiators (launcher mutual-exclusion groups for kiosk/gaming session switching, ZFS, headscale, gamescope/lutris backends, single-device MQTT-only identity) are jupiterOS-native. Supporting signals: github-muniterhalinuxcompanion-homeassistant-linux-companion-github is migrating TO MQTT precisely for last-will semantics (validates ha-linux-agent's transport); wth-there-is-no-windows-and-linux-ha-app-similar-to-macos-month-of-what-the-heck documents the genuinely-open Linux niche; releases-hass-agenthassagent-github shows even the mature HASS.Agent shipped the same rediscovery bug (#230) ha-linux-agent has today. Unresolved and depth-answerable: the exact capability delta against ha-linux-agent's 12 backends; whether go-hass-agent/lnxlink work headless on servers (logind/system-bus sensors should — verify against their issue trackers); whether the incumbents' lack of a NixOS service module (package only, per go-hass-agent-mynixos) is sufficient differentiation for a declarative 7-host fleet; and whether go-hass-agent's commands.toml could emulate launcher groups (states don't sync back — probably not for mutual-exclusion UI).

opposing_positions.position: Adopt: go-hass-agent v14.15.1 is already in nixpkgs (all 24 Linux platforms), actively maintained, sensor-complete, security-mature (per-feature capabilities, cosign); lnxlink is the community-endorsed Linux agent with ~50 modules. ha-linux-agent's differentiation is small against the maintenance burden of a custom 12-crate agent with 3 tests.

Build (fix): ha-linux-agent's jupiterOS-native features are real and unmet — launcher mutual-exclusion groups for kiosk session switching, ZFS/headscale backends, declarative per-host NixOS module integration, MQTT-only single-device identity avoiding go-hass-agent's documented split-brain (device registered twice, mobile_app AND MQTT, cannot be combined).

suggested_searches: go-hass-agent headless server no desktop session
go-hass-agent NixOS systemd service module configuration
lnxlink server host headless systemd
go-hass-agent commands.toml limitations state sync
HASS.Agent satellite service headless pattern

loci.name: mqtt-lifecycle-supervisor-spec
loci.one_line: What is the concrete, implementable MQTT lifecycle supervisor design (reconnect re-subscription, birth-triggered rediscovery with jitter, availability/LWT, stale-message bounding, discovery cleanup, and the paired broker-side sizing on callisto) that turns the corpus's consensus WHATs into a phase-1 spec?
loci.rationale: The user's 'never reliable' complaint is the research's centre of gravity, and the corpus has established the WHAT as near-consensus (consensus-claims.json: re-subscribe per rumqttc #250; clean_session=false + stable client_id per librs; birth-triggered rediscovery per HA docs; own offline publish on SIGTERM since LWT never fires on graceful disconnect) — but never assembles the HOW, which is what the roadmap actually needs. Unresolved specifics, each with corpus evidence but no corpus answer: (a) rumqttc exposes NO disconnect callback and no pending-message TTL (rumqttc-reconnection-to-mqtt-broker-and-pending-messages-ttl-issue-211-bytebeami — open since Dec 2020), so what supervisor pattern detects broker loss and bounds stale queued telemetry before HA sees hours-old sensor values; (b) mqtt-home-assistant-3 recommends a random delay on birth-triggered rediscovery to avoid broker IO spikes, and device-availability-zigbee2mqtt shows the production jitter/backoff pattern (30s jitter, ping backoff x1.5/x3/x6/x12, per-class check-in windows) — which pattern fits a 7-host fleet; (c) some-mqtt-devices-unavailable-after-ha-restart-issue-135266-home-assistantcore-2 + comments prove broker max_queued_messages (mosquitto default 1000) SILENTLY drops retained replay at entity scale (5374 entities; 56 of 112 topics arrived empty), so the spec must pair agent behaviour with callisto's actual mosquitto config (depth investigator has jupiter-os ground truth access); (d) librs proves rumqttc at main is MQTT v3.1.1-only, so HA's message_expiry_interval (mqtt-home-assistant-3) is unavailable and ghost-entity cleanup must use the empty-payload retained-topic clearing order the-homie-convention specifies (state first, then attributes) — exactly the failure telegraf2hassio users hit; (e) my-hand-built-mqtt-devices-are-unavailable-after-hassio-restart-but-zigbee2mqtt establishes the retained-discipline matrix (config+state+availability retained, commands never retained) and mqtt-client-component-esphome-smart-home-made-simple adds the shutdown_message and reboot_timeout (15-min self-healing) patterns worth porting; (f) releases-hass-agenthassagent-github (#230 fix) is the precedent showing republish-on-reconnect is the fix shipped by a mature agent for this exact bug class. Deliverable: an implementable supervisor spec — connection states, timers, topic/payload discipline, and the broker-side settings — for roadmap phase 1.
suggested_searches: mosquitto max_queued_messages sizing retained replay
ESPHome birth message republish discovery pattern
MQTT client supervisor pattern reconnect stale message TTL
HA mqtt discovery cleanup empty payload retained remove device
MQTT jitter backoff fleet devices birth message storm

loci.name: rumqttc-dependency-fitness
loci.one_line: Is rumqttc (pinned at 0.24 in this repo) the right dependency to build the reliability phase on: is reconnect re-subscription (#250) actually fixed in any release, what is the crate's real maintenance state, and does its MQTT v3.1.1-only surface force the workarounds in the lifecycle spec — or should the agent switch clients?
loci.rationale: Every phase-1 fix builds on rumqttc, yet the corpus never verifies rumqttc is the right bet. Specific unresolved questions with corpus hooks: (a) automatic-reconnect-and-subscribed-topics-issue-250-bytebeamiorumqtt-github (open since Feb 2021, labelled 'in-pipeline as of #1052') is the agent's exact verified defect — the corpus contains no evidence whether PR #1052 or any release actually shipped re-subscription handling, so the depth investigator must read the rumqtt repo/PR/releases directly; (b) rumqttc-rust shows 0.25.1 docs built 1 Sept 2026 (so the crate is alive) but only 35.34% documented, and 'automatic reconnections by just continuing the poll' is advertised while re-subscription is NOT part of the advertised feature list; (c) rumqttc-reconnection-to-mqtt-broker-and-pending-messages-ttl-issue-211-bytebeami (open, stale/blocked since 2020) shows no disconnect callback and no TTL exists even in design — is that acceptable for a fleet-critical dependency, and what's the workaround contract; (d) librs + rumqttrumqttcsrceventlooprs-at-main-bytebeamiorumqtt-github prove main-branch rumqttc is MQTT v3.1.1-only (mqttbytes::v4 only; clean_session semantics; session_present=false discards pending) — confirm no v5 path exists in any release, which locks out HA's message_expiry_interval and modernises the ghost-entity workaround; (e) what changed between the repo's pinned 0.24 and 0.25.1 (changelog), and what do the alternatives look like (paho.mqtt rust, other maintained crates) against the supervisor requirements of the lifecycle locus; (f) no-keepalive-0-still-allowed-with-max_keepalive-set-issue-2117-eclipse-mosquitto documents the mosquitto-side keepalive constraint (keep_alive must be non-zero on mosquitto v2.0.12+) the client config must respect. Keep-vs-replace changes phase-1 implementation cost and the credibility of 'fix rumqttc usage' vs 'swap client' in the roadmap.
suggested_searches: rumqttc 0.25 release notes changelog
rumqtt PR 1052 resubscribe reconnect merged
rumqttc MQTT 5 support roadmap
rust MQTT client production paho vs rumqttc
rumqttc maintenance status 2026

loci.name: headless-privilege-ladder
loci.one_line: For the server hosts (europa, callisto), which monitoring channel + privilege design per subsystem — SMART via smartd -M exec hooks vs direct privileged ioctls, ZFS via zed events vs zpool polling, systemd unit health via D-Bus signals vs OnFailure= drop-in — and what capability set does the resulting unit need?
loci.rationale: Sub-Q6 breadth is covered, but the per-subsystem channel-and-privilege design is genuinely open, and it feeds back into locus 1's service model (a system unit with AmbientCapabilities= changes the answer). The corpus gestures at each fork without resolving any: (a) disk health — clarification-of-volume-permissions-issue-26-analogjscrutiny-github is kernel-source evidence that NVMe SMART REQUIRES CAP_SYS_ADMIN (NVME_IOCTL_ADMIN_CMD check) while SATA needs only CAP_SYS_RAWIO, so the agent either takes those capabilities, or stays unprivileged and bridges the already-root smartd daemon via -M exec hooks whose SMARTD_MESSAGE/SMARTD_FAILTYPE env-var contract smart-archwiki documents (smartdconf5-smartmontools-debian-testing-debian-manpages carries the full config surface), or follows github-prometheus-communitysmartctl_exporter-export-smartctl-statistics-to-prome's exporter pattern; answers (superuser note) pins the /dev/nvme0 control-node enumeration detail; (b) ZFS on callisto — how-to-monitor-zfs-pool-health-and-status-on-ubuntu documents zed (ZFS Event Daemon) as the event-driven channel plus the threshold script pattern (pool state != ONLINE critical, capacity > 85% warn, CKSUM errors), vs the current backend's zpool polling; (c) systemd unit health — github-joontysystemd_mon-monitor-for-systemd-to-alert-failed-services-github shows the no-polling D-Bus subscription pattern (with its 'who watches the watcher' SIGKILL caveat), see-also-3 (systemd.unit(5) source) documents the global OnFailure=failure-handler@%N drop-in pattern that captures failures fleet-wide with zero agent polling, and systemd-units-monitoring-netdata shows Netdata's unit-collection semantics as a third reference — which channel is NixOS-native and how do they combine; (d) kiosk-side events — ipc-niri-msg-niri documents niri's event-stream (complete state up-front, then incremental) replacing niri msg polling, but the corpus says nothing about reconnect behaviour when the compositor restarts; backlight hotkey changes need a uevent listener (sysfs-class-backlight, backlight-support-the-linux-kernel-documentation) and no note covers a Rust uevent mechanism. The answers determine the europa/callisto feature phase of the roadmap AND the unit's final privilege set.

zed ZFS event daemon custom notify script

loci.name: testing-gate-for-hardware-daemon
loci.one_line: What concrete CI test design actually gates the reliability fixes — ephemeral-broker reconnect simulation, birth-message rediscovery tests without a full HA, a runNixOSTest for the NixOS module, and the zbus session-bus CI workaround — for a workspace currently at 3 tests in 12 crates?
loci.rationale: The verified 3-tests-in-12-crates state means every reliability fix lands with no regression protection, and the roadmap's 'reliability first' phase is hollow without a gate. The corpus has the individual tools but no assembled pattern, and leaves specific questions open: (a) mosquitto-in-testcontainers_modulesmosquitto-rust and github-testcontainerstestcontainers-rs-modules-community-community-maintained-mo (plus testcontainers-mosquitto-module and hivemq-is-now-available-in-testcontainers) document spinning an ephemeral Mosquitto with configurable tags, startup timeouts, and ready conditions — but nothing in the corpus shows the hard part: simulating broker restart/connection loss mid-test to prove re-subscription and rediscovery (the exact bug class); (b) testing birth-triggered rediscovery without a full HA needs a synthetic subscriber/publisher — github-inovexmqtt_blackbox_exporter-prometheus-exporter-for-mqtt-monitoring-gith and mqtt-blackbox-synthetic-testing-learn-netdata gesture at MQTT synthetic testing but nobody applies it to HA discovery semantics; (c) nixos-manual documents runNixOSTest for out-of-tree module testing in QEMU VMs — does nixpkgs already ship a mosquitto or MQTT-related NixOS test the module test can crib from (depth investigator should grep nixpkgs); (d) github-z-galaxyzbus-rust-d-bus-crate-github shows the crate assumes DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS, the known CI constraint for D-Bus tests — what is the documented workaround (dbus-daemon per-test? testcontainers?); (e) mocking-stdfs-for-unit-tests-help-the-rust-programming-language-forum and tempfile-rust give the hermetic-file pattern for sysfs-touching code (trait abstraction + tempdir), which the hardware backend's fake-options defect shows is missing; (f) what the gate should enforce (clippy already failing on backend-hardware map_or per ground truth; coverage targets per crate). Lower disagreement but phase-gating: without this locus the roadmap's phase 1 has no definition of done.

nixpkgs nixos/tests mosquitto test
runNixOSTest out-of-tree module example
zbus tests DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS CI dbus-daemon
rust integration test MQTT reconnect re-subscribe

skip_loci.reason: Substantially resolved for THIS fleet by the corpus, so a standalone depth locus would re-read known evidence. github-muniterhalinuxcompanion documents the native-API agent migrating TO MQTT precisely because it cannot reflect a host going offline; the wth-there-is-no-windows-and-linux-ha-app thread records that HASS.Agent needs MQTT for most features and that a community mod calls MQTT 'more native than many things'; github-gamerclassn7 shows the MQTT-free native-API counter-architecture exists but its author points Linux users elsewhere; koying's metrics-fidelity counter-position (system-design-architecting-ha-data-flows) is moot for jupiterOS — no corpus evidence the fleet runs InfluxDB, and the user's stated needs (HA automations, dashboards, kiosk control) are exactly the bidirectional MQTT use case. The one genuinely open fragment inside this cluster — rumqttc's own fitness, v3.1.1-only surface, and client alternatives — is promoted to its own locus, rumqttc-dependency-fitness.

The contradiction graph itself states the reconciliation (hybrid: poll cheap sysfs/procfs scalars on interval, subscribe where kernel/D-Bus events exist), and both sides' evidence is architectural-primary on both sides. A standalone locus would mostly confirm the known reconciliation. The genuinely open per-subsystem specifics — D-Bus signals vs OnFailure= drop-in for unit health, zed for ZFS, smartd -M exec for disks, uevents for backlight sync, niri event-stream reconnection — are absorbed into headless-privilege-ladder where they interact with the privilege decision that actually shapes the roadmap.

Already refuted at consensus level (consensus-claims.json): Telegraf's MQTT output cannot produce HA discovery, cannot set a dynamic LWT, and has 'very limited' lifecycle management (telegrafpluginsoutputsmqttreadmemd evidence); the Glances HA integration has a 6-year record of silent-failure modes (glances-integration-loses-connection, glances-sensors-are-renamed, cannot-access-glances); Netdata's default footprint (100-350MB, documented blowups in insane-netdata-memory-usage) is disqualified for kiosk fleet deployment; HA's Prometheus integration is export-only (prometheus-home-assistant). Depth would re-read what the corpus already settles. The live build-vs-buy question is agent-vs-agent (go-hass-agent, lnxlink), which is the adopt-vs-build-verdict locus.

Real but secondary: the verified dead tls config knob and MQTT-credential delivery matter, but the corpus has no contested material on it (nixos-manual documents mosquitto ACL/TLS listener options; flakes-official-nixos-wiki documents the store-is-world-readable warning) — it is an engineering task, not an uncertain question. Folded into fleet-service-model-by-host-class as sub-question (d): the module shape determines how credentials/TLS reach the agent on every host, and the depth investigator for that locus has jupiter-os ground-truth access to see how callisto's broker and the kiosks are wired today.
